summary: Accra is the spiritual home of the African-American diaspora return movement, with well-developed expat zones and a genuinely welcoming culture. Phone snatching is the most common risk and requires consistent awareness. Violent crime against foreigners is rare in the main diaspora zones of East Legon, Cantonments, and Airport Residential. The city is navigable with standard urban awareness. The northern border regions have an entirely different and elevated risk profile.
dataSource: US State Dept, UK FCO, Numbeo 2025, OSAC

usDeptState.label: Exercise Increased Caution
usDeptState.summary: Exercise increased caution in Ghana due to crime and civil unrest. Violent crime such as carjackings, home invasions, and armed robbery occur. Northern regions near Burkina Faso border are Level 3.

ukFco.summary: Exercise a high degree of caution in Ghana. Ongoing risk of violent crime and petty crime throughout. Northern border regions flagged separately at higher risk.

crimeTypes: Phone snatching (very common citywide: keep all devices out of sight)
Express kidnapping (rare; primarily affecting high-profile local targets)
currentAlerts: Northern regions: Upper East and Upper West provinces are Level 3 (Reconsider Travel) due to Sahel terrorism spillover from Burkina Faso. Accra is unaffected.
Sporadic civil unrest possible around political events and elections. Monitor local news around election periods.
Phone snatching is high frequency in the CBD and markets. Keep all devices in your pocket or bag at all times.
January 2025 advisory update maintained Level 2 for Accra.
safetyTips: Use only Uber or Bolt. Never enter unmarked taxis. 'One-chance' taxi robberies are a known risk.
Keep your phone inside your pocket or bag at all times in public. Phone snatching is the single most common crime.
Do not walk at night in markets, the CBD, or Accra New Town.
In East Legon and Airport Residential, standard precautions are sufficient.
To report a crime or summon police in Ghana, call 191 (Police Emergency). For ambulance services call 193. For fire call 192. Save these numbers in your phone before you arrive.
If you witness or are involved in a serious incident, you can also reach the Tourist Police helpline at 0800 111 500 (toll-free). They are specifically trained to assist visitors.

US citizens contact the U.S. Embassy Accra for emergency consular assistance at +233 030 274 1000. UK nationals contact the British High Commission Accra at +233 302 213 250. Both have 24-hour emergency lines.
Carry a photocopy of your passport. Original stays secured at your accommodation.
Enroll in the US Embassy Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) at step.state.gov before your trip to receive automatic security alerts for Ghana.
keyFacts: Most popular diaspora return destination in Africa. Well-developed expat zones with strong community networks.
Northern border provinces have Level 3 US advisory. Accra itself is Level 2.
Ghana's Right of Abode program for African diaspora makes it one of the most welcoming cities in this directory.
English is the official language, reducing communication friction with police and authorities.
SafetyWing and similar travel insurance is strongly recommended for all visits.
highlights: English-speaking city with strong diaspora infrastructure
Well-established safe expat zones (East Legon, Cantonments)
Violent crime against foreigners rare in main diaspora areas
Active tourism police and diaspora support networks
challenges: Phone snatching epidemic requires constant vigilance
Northern border regions have significantly elevated risk
